Petra crafts a piece of jewellery out of two black and two white hearts. The hearts have areas of $1 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}, 4 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}, 9 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$ and $16 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$ respectively. She places the hearts on top of each other as shown in the diagram and glues them together. How big is the total area of the visible black parts?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The four heart shapes in the image are concentrically nested and stacked, with the colors from outside to inside being black, white, black, white in order. That is to say, the visible black parts include one ring of the outermost black heart, as well as one ring of the smaller black heart in the middle; each black heart is partially covered by the adjacent white heart above it. Reasoning: The problem gives the areas of the four heart shapes as 1, 4, 9, 16 cm^2 respectively. According to the sizes in the image, from inside to outside they correspond to 1, 4, 9, 16 cm^2. The outer black heart has area 16 cm^2 and is covered by the white heart with area 9 cm^2, so the visible black area of the outer layer is 16 - 9 = 7 cm^2. The inner black heart has area 4 cm^2 and is covered by the white heart with area 1 cm^2, so the visible black area of the inner layer is 4 - 1 = 3 cm^2. The total visible black area is 7 + 3 = 10 cm^2.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the four hearts are nested concentrically, with colors from outside to inside: black, white, black, white. Read from the text that their areas are 1, 4, 9, and 16 cm^2, so assign these by size from inner to outer: 1, 4, 9, 16. The visible black part consists of the outer black heart not covered by the white heart on top, plus the inner black heart not covered by the smallest white heart. Compute these as (16 - 9) + (4 - 1) = 7 + 3 = 10 cm^2.
